I will mostly follow what I did last year, because on 5 mu I cannot afford fancy experiments. I grow winter wheat and summer maize in the same land, so I look at the whole year together. If I spend too much on one crop, the other one suffers. I have well irrigation, so I do not want the field to go short of water at the key stages. On fertilizer, I would rather put a little extra than watch the crop turn pale and lose yield. Around here, if wheat has enough base fertilizer and two or three good waterings, it usually stands well. For maize, I do the same way many people here do: use hybrid seed, feed it mainly with nitrogen, and do not leave phosphorus too low because the roots need to start fast after wheat harvest. I will keep wheat on improved seed, maize on hybrid seed, use rotary tillage for speed and labor saving, and hold pesticide sprays to the common problems, not spray blindly. With my land size and family labor, this is the safest way to keep output steady.
